sanskrit: karṇa uvāca svavīrye 'haṃ parāśvasya prārthayāmy arjunaṃ raṇe tvaṃ tu mitramukhaḥ śatrur māṃ bhīṣayitum icchasi
english: Karṇa said: Trusting in my own valor I challenge Arjuna in battle. But you, an enemy wearing a friend's face, wish only to frighten me.

sanskrit: na mām asmād abhiprāyāt kaś cid adya nivartayet apīndro vajram udyamya kiṃ nu martyaḥ kariṣyati
english: No one today shall turn me back from this resolve—not even Indra, raising his thunderbolt. What then can a mere mortal do?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca iti karṇasya vākyānte śalyaḥ prāhottaraṃ vacaḥ cukopayiṣur atyarthaṃ karṇaṃ madreśvaraḥ punaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When Karṇa's speech was ended, Śalya, the lord of the Madras, spoke his reply again, eager to provoke Karṇa to the utmost.

sanskrit: yadā vai tvāṃ phalgunaveganunnā; jyācoditā hastavatā visṛṣṭāḥ anvetāraḥ kaṅkapatrāḥ śitāgrās; tadā tapsyasy arjunasyābhiyogāt
english: When the heron-feathered arrows, sped by Phalguna's force, loosed from the bowstring by his skilled hand, their points whetted sharp, come pursuing you—then you shall burn with grief at Arjuna's onslaught.

sanskrit: yadā divyaṃ dhanur ādāya pārthaḥ; prabhāsayan pṛtanāṃ savyasācī tvām ardayeta niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkais; tadā paścāt tapsyase sūtaputra
english: When Pārtha, the ambidextrous archer, taking up his divine bow and lighting up the whole army, crushes you with his keen shafts—then, son of a charioteer, you shall repent too late.

sanskrit: bālaś candraṃ mātur aṅke śayāno; yathā kaś cit prārthayate 'pahartum tadvan mohād yatamāno rathasthas; tvaṃ prārthayasy arjunam adya jetum
english: As a child lying in its mother's lap reaches out to seize the moon, so you, standing on your chariot and striving in your folly, long today to conquer Arjuna.

sanskrit: triśūlam āśliṣya sutīkṣṇadhāraṃ; sarvāṇi gātrāṇi nigharṣasi tvam sutīkṣṇadhāropamakarmaṇā tvaṃ; yuyutsase yo 'rjunenādya karṇa
english: Embracing a trident of razor-keen edge, you rub all your limbs against it—for, Karṇa, in seeking to fight Arjuna today you face a deed sharp as that very edge.

sanskrit: siddhaṃ siṃhaṃ kesariṇaṃ bṛhantaṃ; bālo mūḍhaḥ kṣudramṛgas tarasvī samāhvayet tadvad etat tavādya; samāhvānaṃ sūtaputrārjunasya
english: As a young, foolish, headstrong little beast might challenge a great, full-grown, maned lion—such, son of a charioteer, is your challenge to Arjuna today.

sanskrit: mā sūtaputrāhvaya rājaputraṃ; mahāvīryaṃ kesariṇaṃ yathaiva vane sṛgālaḥ piśitasya tṛpto; mā pārtham āsādya vinaṅkṣyasi tvam
english: Do not, O son of a charioteer, challenge that prince of mighty valor, as a jackal in the forest, gorged on flesh, might challenge a lion—do not perish by approaching Pārtha.

sanskrit: īṣādantaṃ mahānāgaṃ prabhinnakaraṭāmukham śaśakāhvayase yuddhe karṇa pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: You, a hare, summon to battle a great elephant whose tusks are like chariot-poles and whose temples and mouth run with rut—you summon Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya, O Karṇa.

sanskrit: bilasthaṃ kṛṣṇasarpaṃ tvaṃ bālyāt kāṣṭhena vidhyasi mahāviṣaṃ pūrṇakośaṃ yat pārthaṃ yoddhum icchasi
english: In your childishness you poke with a stick at a black serpent lying in its hole—a creature of deadly venom, its poison-sac brimful—when you wish to fight Pārtha.

sanskrit: siṃhaṃ kesariṇaṃ kruddham atikramyābhinardasi sṛgāla iva mūḍhatvān nṛsiṃhaṃ karṇa pāṇḍavam
english: In your folly you cross the path of a wrathful maned lion and roar at him like a jackal—at Pāṇḍava, that lion among men, O Karṇa.

sanskrit: suparṇaṃ patagaśreṣṭhaṃ vainateyaṃ tarasvinam laṭvevāhvayase pāte karṇa pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Like a small bird you summon to the swoop the fair-winged son of Vinatā, swiftest and best of all that fly—you summon Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya, O Karṇa.

sanskrit: sarvāmbhonilayaṃ bhīmam ūrmimantaṃ jhaṣāyutam candrodaye vivartantam aplavaḥ saṃtitīrṣasi
english: Without a boat you would cross the dread abode of all waters, surging with waves and teeming with great fish, swelling at the rising of the moon.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhaṃ dundubhigrīvaṃ tīkṣṇaśṛṅgaṃ prahāriṇam vatsa āhvayase yuddhe karṇa pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Like a calf you summon to combat a bull with a neck deep as a drum, sharp-horned and ready to strike—you summon Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya, O Karṇa.

sanskrit: mahāghoṣaṃ mahāmeghaṃ darduraḥ pratinardasi kāmatoyapradaṃ loke naraparjanyam arjunam
english: Like a frog you croak back at a great thundering cloud—at Arjuna, that rain-god among men, who pours upon the world the waters of every wish.

sanskrit: yathā ca svagṛhasthaḥ śvā vyāghraṃ vanagataṃ bhaṣet tathā tvaṃ bhaṣase karṇa naravyāghraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: As a dog kept in its own house might bark at a tiger ranging in the forest, so do you bark, O Karṇa, at Dhanaṃjaya, that tiger among men.

sanskrit: sṛgālo 'pi vane karṇa śaśaiḥ parivṛto vasan manyate siṃham ātmānaṃ yāvat siṃhaṃ na paśyati
english: A jackal too, O Karṇa, dwelling in the forest surrounded by hares, thinks himself a lion—so long as he has not yet seen a lion.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api rādheya siṃham ātmānam icchasi apaśyañ śatrudamanaṃ naravyāghraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Just so, son of Rādhā, you imagine yourself a lion—having not yet beheld Dhanaṃjaya, that subduer of foes, that tiger among men.

sanskrit: vyāghraṃ tvaṃ manyase ''tmānaṃ yāvat kṛṣṇau na paśyasi samāsthitāv ekarathe sūryācandramasāv iva
english: You think yourself a tiger only so long as you have not seen the two Kṛṣṇas standing together upon one chariot, like the sun and the moon.

sanskrit: yāvad gāṇḍīvanirghoṣaṃ na śṛṇoṣi mahāhave tāvad eva tvayā karṇa śakyaṃ vaktuṃ yathecchasi
english: Only so long as you have not heard the roar of Gāṇḍīva in the great battle, O Karṇa, can you speak as you please.

sanskrit: rathaśabdadhanuḥśabdair nādayantaṃ diśo daśa nardantam iva śārdūlaṃ dṛṣṭvā kroṣṭā bhaviṣyasi
english: When you behold him making the ten directions ring with the din of his chariot and bow, roaring like a tiger, you will turn into a jackal.

sanskrit: nityam eva sṛgālas tvaṃ nityaṃ siṃho dhanaṃjayaḥ vīrapradveṣaṇān mūḍha nityaṃ kroṣṭeva lakṣyase
english: You are ever a jackal, and Dhanaṃjaya is ever a lion. Fool, through your hatred of the brave you appear forever as a jackal.

sanskrit: yathākhuḥ syād biḍālaś ca śvā vyāghraś ca balābale yathā sṛgālaḥ siṃhaś ca yathā ca śaśakuñjarau
english: As the mouse to the cat, the dog to the tiger, in strength and weakness; as the jackal to the lion, as the hare to the elephant—

sanskrit: yathānṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca yathā cāpi viṣāmṛte tathā tvam api pārthaś ca prakhyātāv ātmakarmabhiḥ
english: as falsehood to truth, as poison to the nectar of immortality—so are you and Pārtha, each made known by your own deeds.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca adhikṣiptas tu rādheyaḥ śalyenāmitatejasā śalyam āha susaṃkruddho vākśalyam avadhārayan
english: Saṃjaya said: But the son of Rādhā, thus reviled by Śalya of boundless splendor, in towering rage answered Śalya, fixing in his mind that spear of words.

sanskrit: guṇān guṇavataḥ śalya guṇavān vetti nāguṇaḥ tvaṃ tu nityaṃ guṇair hīnaḥ kiṃ jñāsyasy aguṇo guṇān
english: The virtues of a man of virtue, O Śalya, are known by one who has virtue, not by one without it. But you, ever destitute of merit, how shall you, the meritless, know merit?

sanskrit: arjunasya mahāstrāṇi krodhaṃ vīryaṃ dhanuḥ śarān ahaṃ śalyābhijānāmi na tvaṃ jānāsi tat tathā
english: Arjuna's mighty weapons, his wrath, his valor, his bow and arrows—these I know well, O Śalya; you do not know them so.

sanskrit: evam evātmano vīryam ahaṃ vīryaṃ ca pāṇḍave jānann evāhvaye yuddhe śalya nāgniṃ pataṃgavat
english: Knowing thus both my own valor and the valor that is in the Pāṇḍava, I challenge him to battle, O Śalya—not like a moth rushing into the fire.

sanskrit: asti cāyam iṣuḥ śalya supuṅkho raktabhojanaḥ ekatūṇīśayaḥ patrī sudhautaḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ
english: And here, O Śalya, is this arrow, finely nocked, drinker of blood, lying apart in its own quiver, well-feathered, burnished bright and richly adorned.

sanskrit: śete candanapūrṇena pūjito bahulāḥ samāḥ āheyo viṣavān ugro narāśvadvipasaṃghahā
english: It has rested, honored, for many long years in a casket filled with sandal-paste—venomous as a serpent, deadly, the slayer of hosts of men, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: ekavīro mahāraudras tanutrāsthividāraṇaḥ nirbhindyāṃ yena ruṣṭo 'ham api meruṃ mahāgirim
english: Peerless among shafts, of terrible might, it cleaves armor and bone alike; with it, in my fury, I could rive even Meru, the great mountain.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ jātu nāsyeyam anyasmin phalgunād ṛte kṛṣṇād vā devakīputrāt satyaṃ cātra śṛṇuṣva me
english: This shaft I would never loose at any other than Phalguna, or Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī—hear from me the truth of this.

sanskrit: tenāham iṣuṇā śalya vāsudevadhanaṃjayau yotsye paramasaṃkruddhas tat karma sadṛśaṃ mama
english: With that arrow, O Śalya, in utmost wrath I shall fight Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya—such a deed is worthy of me.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ vāsudevānāṃ kṛṣṇe lakṣmīḥ pratiṣṭhitā sarveṣāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ jayaḥ pārthe pratiṣṭhitaḥ ubhayaṃ tat samāsādya ko 'tivartitum arhati
english: In Kṛṣṇa rests the glory of all the Vāsudevas, and in Pārtha rests the victory of all the sons of Pāṇḍu. Who, meeting both together, could hope to overcome them?

sanskrit: tāv etau puruṣavyāghrau sametau syandane sthitau mām ekam abhisaṃyātau sujātaṃ śalya paśya me
english: When these two tigers among men, standing together upon one chariot, advance against me alone—then, O Śalya, behold the noble deed that is mine.

sanskrit: pitṛṣvasāmātulajau bhrātarāv aparājitau maṇī sūtra iva protau draṣṭāsi nihatau mayā
english: Those two cousins, sons of a father's sister and a mother's brother, unconquered kinsmen—you shall see them slain by me, strung like two gems upon a single thread.

sanskrit: arjune gāṇḍivaṃ kṛṣṇe cakraṃ tārkṣyakapidhvajau bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajananau śalya harṣakarau mama
english: In Arjuna is the Gāṇḍīva, in Kṛṣṇa the discus; the one bears Garuḍa, the other the monkey on his banner. These two, terror to the timid, bring me joy, O Śalya.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu duṣprakṛtir mūḍho mahāyuddheṣv akovidaḥ bhayāvatīrṇaḥ saṃtrāsād abaddhaṃ bahu bhāṣase
english: But you, of base nature, a fool unskilled in great battles, sunk in fear, out of sheer terror babble much that is incoherent.

sanskrit: saṃstauṣi tvaṃ tu kenāpi hetunā tau kudeśaja tau hatvā samare hantā tvām addhā sahabāndhavam
english: For some reason you sing the praises of those two, O man of a vile land. When I have slain them in battle, I shall surely slay you too, along with your kinsmen.

sanskrit: pāpadeśaja durbuddhe kṣudra kṣatriyapāṃsana suhṛd bhūtvā ripuḥ kiṃ māṃ kṛṣṇābhyāṃ bhīṣayann asi
english: Born of a sinful land, dull-witted, base, you disgrace of warriors—having been a friend, why now, turned enemy, do you seek to frighten me with the two Kṛṣṇas?

sanskrit: tau vā mamādya hantārau hantāsmi samare sthitau nāhaṃ bibhemi kṛṣṇābhyāṃ vijānann ātmano balam
english: Either those two shall slay me today, or I shall slay them as they stand in battle. I do not fear the two Kṛṣṇas, for I know full well my own strength.

sanskrit: vāsudevasahasraṃ vā phalgunānāṃ śatāni ca aham eko haniṣyāmi joṣam āssva kudeśaja
english: Were there a thousand Vāsudevas and hundreds of Phalgunas, I alone would slay them all. Hold your peace, O man of a wretched land.

sanskrit: striyo bālāś ca vṛddhāś ca prāyaḥ krīḍāgatā janāḥ yā gāthāḥ saṃpragāyanti kurvanto 'dhyayanaṃ yathā tā gāthāḥ śṛṇu me śalya madrakeṣu durātmasu
english: Hear from me, O Śalya, those verses about the vile Madrakas which women, children, the old, and folk gathered at play sing aloud, as though reciting a lesson.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiḥ kathitāḥ pūrvaṃ yathāvad rājasaṃnidhau śrutvā caikamanā mūḍha kṣama vā brūhi vottaram
english: Recited of old by brāhmaṇas, duly, in the presence of a king—listen to them with attention, O fool, and either endure them or make your reply.

sanskrit: mitradhruṅ madrako nityaṃ yo no dveṣṭi sa madrakaḥ madrake saṃgataṃ nāsti kṣudravākye narādhame
english: The Madraka is ever a betrayer of friends; whoever hates us, he is a Madraka. There is no friendship to be had with a Madraka, that basest of men, foul of speech.

sanskrit: durātmā madrako nityaṃ nityaṃ cānṛtiko 'nṛjuḥ yāvadantaṃ hi daurātmyaṃ madrakeṣv iti naḥ śrutam
english: The Madraka is forever vile of soul, forever false and crooked. To the very end there is wickedness among the Madrakas—so have we heard.

sanskrit: pitā mātā ca putraś ca śvaśrūśvaśuramātulāḥ jāmātā duhitā bhrātā naptā te te ca bāndhavāḥ
english: Father and mother and son, mother-in-law, father-in-law, and maternal uncles, son-in-law, daughter, brother, grandson, and all their kindred—

sanskrit: vayasyābhyāgatāś cānye dāsīdāsaṃ ca saṃgatam puṃbhir vimiśrā nāryaś ca jñātājñātāḥ svayecchayā
english: and friends and chance-come guests, men-servants and maid-servants assembled together—and women mingling with men, known and unknown alike, at their own pleasure.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ gṛheṣu śiṣṭānāṃ saktumanthāśināṃ sadā pītvā sīdhuṃ sagomāṃsaṃ nardanti ca hasanti ca
english: In whose houses the so-called respectable, ever feeding on parched barley-meal, having drunk strong liquor together with beef, roar aloud and laugh—

sanskrit: yāni caivāpy abaddhāni pravartante ca kāmataḥ kāmapralāpino 'nyonyaṃ teṣu dharmaḥ kathaṃ bhavet
english: and where unbridled things go on at every whim, where they prattle wantonly to one another—among such people how can there be any righteousness?

sanskrit: madrakeṣu vilupteṣu prakhyātāśubhakarmasu nāpi vairaṃ na sauhārdaṃ madrakeṣu samācaret
english: With the Madrakas, a lawless folk notorious for foul deeds, one should practice neither enmity nor friendship.

sanskrit: madrake saṃgataṃ nāsti madrako hi sacāpalaḥ madrakeṣu ca duḥsparśaṃ śaucaṃ gāndhārakeṣu ca
english: There is no fellowship with a Madraka, for the Madraka is fickle; among the Madrakas, and among the Gāndhārakas, purity is a thing hard to come by.

sanskrit: rājayājakayājyena naṣṭaṃ dattaṃ havir bhavet
english: By an offering performed for a priest who sacrifices for kings, the oblation given is utterly lost.

sanskrit: śūdrasaṃskārako vipro yathā yāti parābhavam tathā brahmadviṣo nityaṃ gacchantīha parābhavam
english: As a brāhmaṇa who performs the sacraments for a śūdra comes to ruin, so do the haters of the brahman ever come to ruin in this world.

sanskrit: madrake saṃgataṃ nāsti hataṃ vṛścikato viṣam ātharvaṇena mantreṇa sarvā śāntiḥ kṛtā bhavet
english: There is no fellowship with a Madraka. The venom of a scorpion's sting is undone, and all is set at peace, by a spell of the Atharvan.

sanskrit: iti vṛścikadaṣṭasya nānāviṣahatasya ca kurvanti bheṣajaṃ prājñāḥ satyaṃ tac cāpi dṛśyate evaṃ vidvañ joṣam āssva śṛṇu cātrottaraṃ vacaḥ
english: For one stung by a scorpion, or stricken by venoms of every kind, the wise prepare a remedy, and its truth is seen indeed. So, knowing this, hold your peace—and yet hear my further word.

sanskrit: vāsāṃsy utsṛjya nṛtyanti striyo yā madyamohitāḥ mithune 'saṃyatāś cāpi yathākāmacarāś ca tāḥ tāsāṃ putraḥ kathaṃ dharmaṃ madrako vaktum arhati
english: Their women, drunk with liquor, cast off their garments and dance, unrestrained in coupling and roaming at their own desire. How can a Madraka, son of such women, presume to speak of righteousness?

sanskrit: yās tiṣṭhantyaḥ pramehanti yathaivoṣṭrīdaśerake tāsāṃ vibhraṣṭalajjānāṃ nirlajjānāṃ tatas tataḥ tvaṃ putras tādṛśīnāṃ hi dharmaṃ vaktum ihecchasi
english: They who make water standing, like she-camels at Daśeraka—you who are the son of such women, fallen from shame and shameless every way, do you wish here to speak of righteousness?

sanskrit: suvīrakaṃ yācyamānā madrakā kaṣati sphijau adātukāmā vacanam idaṃ vadati dāruṇam
english: When a Madraka woman is asked for sūvīraka, she scratches her buttocks; and unwilling to give it, she utters this harsh word:

sanskrit: mā mā suvīrakaṃ kaś cid yācatāṃ dayito mama putraṃ dadyāṃ pratipadaṃ na tu dadyāṃ suvīrakam
english: "Let no one, no one ask me for sūvīraka, which is dear to me. I would sooner give my son for the asking than give up my sūvīraka."

sanskrit: nāryo bṛhatyo nirhrīkā madrakāḥ kambalāvṛtāḥ ghasmarā naṣṭaśaucāś ca prāya ity anuśuśruma
english: The Madraka women are tall and brazen, wrapped in coarse blankets, gluttonous and devoid of all cleanliness—so, for the most part, have we heard.

sanskrit: evamādi mayānyair vā śakyaṃ vaktuṃ bhaved bahu ā keśāgrān nakhāgrāc ca vaktavyeṣu kuvartmasu
english: Of such things, and of others, much could be told by me or by another—of those followers of evil ways, who are blameworthy from the tips of their hair to the tips of their nails.

sanskrit: madrakāḥ sindhusauvīrā dharmaṃ vidyuḥ kathaṃ tv iha pāpadeśodbhavā mlecchā dharmāṇām avicakṣaṇāḥ
english: How then should the Madrakas and the Sindhu-Sauvīras know righteousness here—barbarians sprung from a sinful land, ignorant of all the laws?

sanskrit: eṣa mukhyatamo dharmaḥ kṣatriyasyeti naḥ śrutam yad ājau nihataḥ śete sadbhiḥ samabhipūjitaḥ
english: This, we have heard, is the foremost duty of a warrior: that he lie slain in battle, honored by the good.

sanskrit: āyudhānāṃ saṃparāye yan mucyeyam ahaṃ tataḥ na me sa prathamaḥ kalpo nidhane svargam icchataḥ
english: That I should come free from the clash of arms in the encounter—that is no first choice of mine, who in death desire heaven.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ priyaḥ sakhā cāsmi dhārtarāṣṭrasya dhīmataḥ tadarthe hi mama prāṇā yac ca me vidyate vasu
english: I am the dear friend of the wise son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; for his sake are my very life-breaths, and whatever wealth is mine.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ tvam apy upahitaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ pāpadeśaja yathā hy amitravat sarvaṃ tvam asmāsu pravartase
english: It is plain that you too, O man of a sinful land, have been suborned by the Pāṇḍavas, for you behave toward us in all things like an enemy.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ na khalu śakyo 'haṃ tvadvidhānāṃ śatair api saṃgrāmād vimukhaḥ kartuṃ dharmajña iva nāstikaiḥ
english: Yet surely I cannot be turned away from battle, even by hundreds of your kind—any more than a man who knows the law can be turned by unbelievers.

sanskrit: sāraṅga iva gharmārtaḥ kāmaṃ vilapa śuṣya ca nāhaṃ bhīṣayituṃ śakyaḥ kṣatravṛtte vyavasthitaḥ
english: Like a cātaka bird tormented by the heat, lament and wither away as you please; I, who stand firm in the warrior's calling, cannot be frightened.

sanskrit: tanutyajāṃ nṛsiṃhānām āhaveṣv anivartinām yā gatir guruṇā prāṅ me proktā rāmeṇa tāṃ smara
english: Remember the goal which my teacher Rāma once declared to me—the goal of those lions among men who give up their bodies and never turn back in battle.

sanskrit: sveṣāṃ trāṇārtham udyuktaṃ vadhāya dviṣatām api viddhi mām āsthitaṃ vṛttaṃ paurūravasam uttamam
english: Know that I have taken up that noblest course, the way of Purūravas—bent on the protection of my own and on the slaughter of my foes.

sanskrit: na tad bhūtaṃ prapaśyāmi triṣu lokeṣu madraka yo mām asmād abhiprāyād vārayed iti me matiḥ
english: I see no being in the three worlds, O Madraka, who could turn me back from this resolve—such is my conviction.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidvañ joṣam āssva trāsāt kiṃ bahu bhāṣase mā tvā hatvā pradāsyāmi kravyādbhyo madrakādhama
english: Knowing this, hold your peace. Why, out of fear, do you talk so much? Take care that I do not slay you and cast you to the flesh-eating beasts, O basest of Madrakas.

sanskrit: mitrapratīkṣayā śalya dhārtarāṣṭrasya cobhayoḥ apavādatitikṣābhis tribhir etair hi jīvasi
english: It is only by these three things, O Śalya—out of regard for friendship, for the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and through forbearance toward your abuse—that you yet live.

sanskrit: punaś ced īdṛśaṃ vākyaṃ madrarāja vadiṣyasi śiras te pātayiṣyāmi gadayā vajrakalpayā
english: If once more, O king of the Madras, you speak such a word, I shall strike off your head with my mace, that is like the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śrotāras tv idam adyeha draṣṭāro vā kudeśaja karṇaṃ vā jaghnatuḥ kṛṣṇau karṇo vāpi jaghāna tau
english: This very day, O man of a wretched land, men shall hear and behold whether the two Kṛṣṇas have slain Karṇa, or Karṇa has slain them.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu rādheyaḥ punar eva viśāṃ pate abravīn madrarājānaṃ yāhi yāhīty asaṃbhramam
english: Having spoken thus, O lord of peoples, the son of Rādhā once more said to the king of the Madras, calmly: "Drive on, drive on!"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca māriṣādhiratheḥ śrutvā vaco yuddhābhinandinaḥ śalyo 'bravīt punaḥ karṇaṃ nidarśanam udāharan
english: Saṃjaya said: My lord, having heard the words of the son of Adhiratha, who gloried in battle, Śalya spoke again to Karṇa, putting forth a parable.

sanskrit: yathaiva matto madyena tvaṃ tathā na ca vā tathā tathāhaṃ tvāṃ pramādyantaṃ cikitsāmi suhṛttayā
english: Even as a man is drunk with liquor, so are you—and yet perhaps not quite so; and seeing you thus heedless, I try, out of friendship, to set you right.
